title: Engine Controls — Thrust Lever Assembly — Install the Compatible Friction Seal and the Landed Quadrant Clamp
abstract: Replaces the thrust lever quadrant friction seal and clamp with the compatible pair, restoring breakout force to the delivered range and doubling the lubrication interval.

sections.planning_reason: Crews on aircraft past three years in service reported notchy thrust levers, needing a deliberate push to start moving. Measurement on eleven aircraft showed breakout force rising from eighteen newtons to as much as thirty-four, improving briefly after each lubrication. The seal in the quadrant swells in contact with the specified lubricant, which produces the step in the force and returns as soon as the lubricant is reapplied.
sections.description: This bulletin replaces the friction seal with one in a compound compatible with the specified lubricant and the quadrant clamp with the landed variant that sets seal compression by geometry rather than by clamp torque. The rivets at the clamp interface are replaced with the current standard. The lever geometry, the resolver pick-off and the disconnect switch are unchanged, so no re-rigging is required.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the pedestal and disconnect electrical power at the thrust lever assembly. Record the as-found breakout force at both levers with the gauge and enter it on the reply form. Remove the quadrant clamp and the friction seal, clean the quadrant faces and remove all traces of the previous lubricant. Install the new seal, then the landed clamp with the current rivet standard, and apply the specified lubricant sparingly at the points shown. Measure the breakout force again and confirm it is between sixteen and twenty-two newtons at both levers. Do the thrust lever inspection in AMM-M-76-10-11-200-047-A, restore power, check autothrust engagement and disconnect, then close the pedestal.
sections.effectivity_note: Applies to all MERIDIAN-42 and MERIDIAN-46 aircraft delivered before MSN M00456. Both levers must be embodied together; a mixed standard gives a noticeable difference in feel between the two levers, which crews report as a defect.
sections.material_note: Kit contains two friction seals, two landed clamps and the rivet set. The removed seals are returned with the reply form for compound analysis. The specified lubricant is unchanged and is locally held.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled thrust lever lubrication, or within 24 months of the date of this Service Bulletin.

title: Engine Controls — Thrust Lever Assembly — Install the Compatible Friction Seal and the Landed Quadrant Clamp

issue.reason: Extended lubrication interval stated as conditional on both levers being at the compatible seal standard, and the reporting rule for a part-embodied aircraft added.

abstract: Replaces the thrust lever quadrant friction seal and clamp with the compatible pair on both levers, restoring breakout force to the delivered range and doubling the lubrication interval once both levers are at the new standard.

sections.planning_reason: Crews on aircraft past three years in service reported notchy thrust levers, needing a deliberate push to start moving. Measurement on eleven aircraft showed breakout force rising from eighteen newtons to as much as thirty-four, improving briefly after each lubrication. The seal in the quadrant swells in contact with the specified lubricant, which produces the step in the force and returns as soon as the lubricant is reapplied.
sections.description: This bulletin replaces the friction seal with one in a compound compatible with the specified lubricant and the quadrant clamp with the landed variant that sets seal compression by geometry rather than by clamp torque. The rivets at the clamp interface are replaced with the current standard. The lever geometry, the resolver pick-off and the disconnect switch are unchanged, so no re-rigging is required.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the pedestal and disconnect electrical power at the thrust lever assembly. Record the as-found breakout force at both levers with the gauge and enter it on the reply form. Remove the quadrant clamp and the friction seal, clean the quadrant faces and remove all traces of the previous lubricant. Install the new seal, then the landed clamp with the current rivet standard, and apply the specified lubricant sparingly at the points shown. Do the same for the second lever in the same visit; this bulletin is not complete on an aircraft with one lever converted. Measure the breakout force again and confirm it is between sixteen and twenty-two newtons at both levers. Do the thrust lever inspection in AMM-M-76-10-11-200-047-A, restore power, check autothrust engagement and disconnect, then close the pedestal. Record the embodiment against both levers and set the extended lubrication interval only when both are recorded.
sections.effectivity_note: Applies to all MERIDIAN-42 and MERIDIAN-46 aircraft delivered before MSN M00456. Both levers must be embodied together; a mixed standard gives a noticeable difference in feel between the two levers, which crews report as a defect. The extended lubrication interval that this bulletin brings applies only to an aircraft with both levers at the compatible seal standard. An aircraft that is part embodied, for whatever reason, stays on the delivered interval and the delivered acceptance band until the second lever is converted, and must be recorded in the maintenance programme as part embodied rather than as embodied. The interval table itself is in task AMM-M-76-10-11-200-047-A and is keyed to the seal standard, not to this bulletin.
sections.material_note: Kit contains two friction seals, two landed clamps and the rivet set. The removed seals are returned with the reply form for compound analysis. The specified lubricant is unchanged and is locally held.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled thrust lever lubrication, or within 24 months of the date of the original issue of this Service Bulletin. Both levers in the same visit.
